pages.title: Q3 2026 Embroidery Bonus — Northwest Custom Apparel
pages.mainText: 1 Activation bounties Paid per account. No gate, no cap — these start earning from day one. — New embroidery program An account that has never embroidered with us — going back through our full order history, including the old separate cap-embroidery orders. — Won back An account that embroidered with us before but has been quiet for —+ months, and has now come back. Each account counts once it reaches — of embroidery this quarter. Below that it hasn't qualified yet — which is why the dashboard shows you accounts that are close, so you can nudge them over. Repeat orders from existing embroidery customers earn nothing here. That's deliberate. This bonus pays for new and won-back business — not for the reorders that arrive on their own. Your regular commission still applies to everything, as always. Webstore accounts don't count toward this bonus. Those already earn you the online-store commission, so they're paid there instead of here — never both. That includes every Hops N Drops location. 2 Growth rate On top of the bounties. No steps, no ceiling. Once you pass — of your goal, you earn — for every 1% you add. There are no dead spots. Every fraction of a percent above — pays — half a point is —. You are never in a position where the next order earns you nothing, and there is no cap at the top. Why the two goals are different Each goal comes from that rep's own book history — specifically, the average of your last two quarters of embroidery on accounts that count toward this bonus. A single shared number would be unfair in both directions. Those two quarters were recalculated with webstore accounts taken out, so your goal will look lower than the quarterly totals you remember. Nothing was taken away: your embroidery this quarter is measured the same way, so both sides of the comparison moved together. Filtering the revenue while leaving the old goal in place would have made the target unreachable. The rate is paid per percentage point, not per dollar, precisely so the bigger book is not worth more. Finish at 110% of your goal and you earn exactly the same as the other rep finishing at 110% of hers. Your goal is yours alone — built from your own book, not measured against anyone else's. Because the rate pays per percentage point, you and the other rep earn the same amount for the same achievement against your own number. 3 Team kicker Company-wide embroidery, shared equally. You both earn the same amount. —each Company Q3 embroidery hits — Last year's Q3 came in at $298,155, so this is within reach of a normal quarter. —each Company Q3 embroidery hits — A genuine stretch — though Q3 2024 reached $380,036, so we've been there. This one counts everything The kicker measures all company embroidery — every account, every person, webstore orders included. That's deliberately wider than your individual bonus. It's a team number, so everything the shop embroiders counts toward it, including work that isn't yours. Embroidery is our biggest line at 46% of everything we sell, which makes it the clearest single lever on the company's $3M year. 4 What counts Custom Embroidery orders — caps included (they used to be a separate order type; they're the same line now). Invoiced subtotal — before tax and shipping. Same basis as your online-store bonus. Invoiced between July 1 and September 30. An order that ships in late September but invoices in October counts toward Q4 — same rule as the online-store bonus. Accounts assigned to you in ShopWorks. Direct orders only — webstore accounts are paid through the online-store commission instead. Not counted: any account that orders through an InkSoft webstore (those earn you the online-store commission), and contract decorating for other shops. 5 Where to find your numbers Mission Control shows your live bonus at the top of the page: what you've earned so far, how far to the next rung, which accounts paid you, and a ranked list of who to call next — accounts a nudge away from a bounty, customers who used to embroider, and customers who buy everything else from you but have never embroidered. Open Mission Control Figures update through the day as orders invoice. Bonuses are approved and paid on the normal quarterly cycle. Questions about any of this — ask Erik. Rates and goals are set in Caspio and this page reflects the plan as approved for Q3 2026.

pages.title: SEO Strategy - Northwest Custom Apparel
pages.mainText: Living document — the plan of record for NWCA search strategy. Covers teamnwca.com (this app) and nwcustomapparel.net (Mehar's WordPress site) and how they work together without competing. To change it, tell Claude: “update the SEO Strategy page” — and log the change in §9. Admin-only · Last updated July 14, 2026 5 Blog posts published 25 Drafts banked (~6 mo) 3,197 Product pages w/ SEO heads 546 Custom style descriptions 42 SEMrush keywords (baseline) 4.9★ GBP · 187 reviews Snapshot July 14, 2026 — update these when the monthly review runs. On this page 1 · Mission & the two-site model 2 · The lane map 3 · teamnwca.com plan 4 · nwcustomapparel.net plan 5 · Working with Mehar 6 · Shared facts (NAP & claims) 7 · Scoreboard & checkpoints 8 · Reference shelf 9 · Change log 1 Mission & the two-site model NWCA runs two websites, and Google knows they are the same business — both carry sameAs schema pointing at each other and share the same name, address, and phone (entity stitching, live on both sides since July 12, 2026). That is deliberate: it pools brand authority into one knowledge-graph entity. The one consequence that shapes everything: if both sites publish pages chasing the same search query, Google splits ranking strength between them and often ranks neither on page 1. We watched this happen on .net itself — “custom embroidery near me” split across two of its own pages held both on page 2. Across two domains it is worse. So the rule is not “compete gently”; it is never compete at all: every query class has exactly one owner, and the other site links to it. The strategy in one sentence: .net wins the customer’s trust and location (“who does embroidery near me?”) — teamnwca wins the customer’s product decision and order (“which garment, what price?”) — and each site hands the visitor to the other at exactly the moment their question changes. Division of labor: Mehar (umehar56@gmail.com) runs .net per the Recovery Roadmap. Claude runs teamnwca per this page (weekly blog autopilot + product/brand SEO). Erik owns gray-area calls and relays questions between the two. The full doctrine was decided July 13–14, 2026 (“Lane Split v2”) and sent to Mehar as a 4-document packet on July 14. 2 The lane map — who owns which searches Query classOwnerExamples Local & service intent“near me”, “[service] in [city]”, map pack / GBP .net “custom embroidery near me” (8,100/mo) · “screen printing Tacoma” · all city landing pages Educational / how-it-works / craft .net “how does DTG work” · fabric guides · digitizing & thread education · brand care guides Product & stylestyle numbers, brand catalogs, comparisons, use-case picks teamnwca “pc54 vs pc61” · “custom carhartt” · “richardson 112 colors” · “best polos for office teams” Tools, pricing & calculators teamnwca exclusively quote builders · pricing content · cost calculators · roster/size tools · webstores Company story / history / culture .net “since 1977” story · case studies · team & culture Industry angles split .net keeps its wins (HVAC, construction education, aprons/kitchens, gyms, schools). teamnwca takes product-pick posts for uncovered industries (breweries, landscaping, auto shops, marinas…). Unsure → ask Erik first. The 30-second test for any new content idea Is the searcher asking WHERE to get it done, or WHO to trust locally? → .net city/service page. Is the searcher asking HOW something works? → .net educational post. Is the searcher deciding WHICH product/brand to buy, or asking about PRICE? → teamnwca post, brand page, or tool. Could it honestly go either way? → flag to Erik before writing. Two minutes now beats six months of split rankings. Hi-vis / safety, said once: .net owns the educational angle (ANSI class explainers, “WA hi-vis requirements” — excellent post, link it). teamnwca owns the commercial terms (product picks, “hi-vis shirts with company logo”, the safety-stripes program, /custom-safety-apparel). The ~50 near-duplicate hi-vis drafts in .net’s backup get merged into its educational winners — never published standalone. 3 teamnwca.com — the plan Live assets (protect these — don’t churn what works) AssetStateStanding rule Server-rendered /blog + sitemap + Google Search ConsoleLiveMonday autopilot publishes 1 post/week — never burst-publish Product SEO heads — 3,197 styles, method-aware titles (92% specific)LiveNever per-method URLs (doorway-page trap); one page per style, ever Product_Copy overlay — custom descriptions beat SanMar boilerplate546 stylesInsert-only batches; Erik’s Caspio edits always win; ~2,650 tail remaining Brand landing pages — /custom-carhartt, /custom-caps, /custom-safety-apparelLiveCurated grid + real order stats + FAQ schema; no prices in schema (Rule 9) Blog ↔ product-page internal links (/api/blog-product-map)LiveSelf-wiring — new posts appear on product pages automatically, no deploy Entity stitching (sameAs both domains) + GSC verification routeLiveNEVER remove the google9a8d…html route or the schema blocks Monday blog autopilot with two-way collision gateLiveRefuses same-intent .net collisions AND any local/“near me” query drafts Phased plan (mirrors Mehar’s phases so both sites compound) Phase 1 · now → week 3 Cadence & funnel wiring Weekly blog cadence continues (25 drafts banked ≈ 6 months of runway). Publish the Eddie Bauer / North Face premium-jackets post early — it becomes the funnel target for .net’s Eddie Bauer post (118 visits/mo); send Mehar the URL when live. Funnel-target list delivered to Mehar Done Jul 14 Phase 2 · weeks 3–8 Brand pages wave 2 (while Mehar builds city pages) Replicate the /custom-carhartt pattern: /custom-safety-vests (pairs with the CSV405 post + hi-vis copy already seeded), then /custom-polos, then /custom-new-era (106 styles already have custom copy). One page ≈ every 2 weeks; each added to sitemap-pages.xml. Awaiting Erik go Supply Mehar the copy-paste catalog block for every city page he builds (“Browse 3,000+ styles with live pricing → teamnwca.com”). Product_Copy tail batches continue (PA / P&C / District / OGIO / Nike rests). Phase 3 · weeks 6–14 Claim the tool & comparison ground Publish product-anchored versions of the topics .net’s roadmap floated — “screen printing vs embroidery for uniforms” (which garments/styles, link both builders) and “how quoting works” — so Mehar’s Phase 3 links to existing pages instead of building competing ones. AI-search structure on every post: open with a “The short answer” block, direct-answer H2s, FAQ schema on roundups (.net’s 497 AI citations prove the channel). Industry product-pick drafts publish through fall (breweries, landscaping, auto shops, churches, golf, pet businesses… — all banked, all .net-collision-checked). Phase 4 · ongoing Authority & measurement Backlinks: supplier/brand directories (SanMar, Carhartt authorized decorator) list both domains; “since 1977” PR anchored on the catalog/tools angle for teamnwca. .net’s 615 referring domains link teamnwca sitewide (footer — live) — passes authority to the newer domain (AS 7 vs 26). Monthly review with Mehar’s report — see §7. Hard rules (never break) Rule 9 — one pricing engine. No price appears outside it, on either domain. No prices/offers in any JSON-LD schema. Never chase “near me” or city queries — that lane is .net’s recovery plan. Never write educational/craft content — link .net’s explainer instead. Never copy .net text (literal duplicate content tanks both). Check reference/nwcustomapparel-net-blogs/INDEX.md before writing. Slugs never change after publish. One post/week — steady cadence beats dumps. Every post: 3+ product links, one tool CTA, one .net cross-link where a related explainer exists, meta ≤155 chars written for the click. 4 nwcustomapparel.net — Mehar’s recovery plan Summary of the SEMrush/Claude roadmap delivered July 14, 2026 (full doc in the reference shelf). Mehar executes; this is here so anyone can see what the other half of the strategy is doing. The diagnosis Ranking keywords peaked ~15–18K in early 2025, now ~4–5K; ~1,000 visits/mo and falling ~12–16%. ~47% of traffic is the homepage on brand searches; ~35% is informational posts about other brands (Carhartt, Eddie Bauer) — traffic that Google’s helpful-content updates + AI Overviews are structurally eroding and that rarely converts. The commercial/local “money pages” already exist but sit on pages 2–5 — e.g. /custom-embroidery-seattle/ holds 206 keywords yet earns 5 visits/mo. Proof the fix works: the new Bonney Lake local page already pulls 32 visits/mo at ~#10 for “custom embroidery near me” (8,100 searches/mo). His four phases PhaseFocus 1 · Weeks 1–3Fix “near me” cannibalization (one page per city per term) · on-page overhaul of the money pages · add CTAs from top informational posts to commercial pages · refresh the biggest decliners. 2 · Weeks 3–8Local landing-page system to the Bonney Lake standard — rebuild Seattle/Spokane/Portland/Kent, add Tacoma, Milton, Puyallup, Federal Way, Auburn… URL pattern /custom-embroidery-{city}-wa/, 301 old variants · optimize Google Business Profile + citations + reviews. 3 · Weeks 6–14Content triage of ~300 posts (keep/merge/retire; hi-vis drafts merged, not published) · pivot new content to commercial/local/industry topics · keep AI-citation-friendly structure (497 citations today). 4 · OngoingGrow referring domains (615 → competitor benchmark ~1,300) · close keyword gaps vs brokenarrowwear / thefoundryclothing. Anti-doorway rule (his playbook, worth repeating): city pages are NOT find-and-replace clones — each needs ~40–50% genuinely unique local content (real neighborhoods, industries, drive times, local reviews) or Google suppresses the whole set. The Bonney Lake page ranks because it’s genuinely useful. 5 Working with Mehar — the treaty terms Contact & routing Mehar: umehar56@gmail.com. Claude never emails him directly — questions route through Erik (“Erik, please ask Mehar…”), and Mehar’s asks for teamnwca (URLs, cross-link targets, confirmed policy numbers) come back the same way. Gray-area topics stop for Erik’s call before anyone writes. Three amendments to his roadmap (relayed Jul 14) Roadmap itemAmendment “Custom embroidery cost calculator” / “bulk polo pricing”Not on .net. All pricing lives in teamnwca’s one engine (Rule 9). .net covers the process angle and links our quote tools. “Screen printing vs embroidery for uniforms”Coordinate the angle. Method education = his; product-anchored comparison = ours (being built in Phase 3). Cross-link both. /dtg-calculator/ + /order-form/Retire & 301. The calculator publishes DTG prices outside the engine; the order form duplicates a retired system. Four additions to his city-page template Catalog block on every city page — “Browse 3,000+ styles with live pricing → teamnwca.com”. His quote CTA stays primary; this is the browsing path. Local visitor lands on .net, transacts on teamnwca. Brand mentions become links — Carhartt → /custom-carhartt, caps → /custom-caps, hi-vis → /custom-safety-apparel; more as wave 2 ships. NAP is a two-site contract — see §6. Claims must match across sites — turnaround, minimums, same-day options say the same thing everywhere. The funnel map — his posts → our pages .net postVisits/moLinks toStatus /how-to-break-in-carhartt-jacket/161/custom-carharttDone Jul 13 /is-eddie-bauer-a-quality-brand/118Premium-jackets post (publishing early)Queued /cotton-vs-polyester-guide/48/blog/pc54-vs-pc61 (links back already)Mehar to add /dtg-printed-hoodies-heavy-equipment…/—/blog/pc90h-vs-gildan-18500 (links back already)Mehar to add /why-is-carhartt-so-popular/ + /carhartt-alternatives…/31+/custom-carhartt (with his Phase-1 refresh)With refresh Works both ways: every teamnwca post cross-links a relevant .net explainer (standing rule, enforced by the autopilot checklist). Collision protocol Mehar, before writing: check teamnwca.com/blog + brand pages. Buying-intent product topic → keep his angle educational/local + cross-link, or skip. teamnwca (automated), before every publish: the Monday autopilot searches .net’s live content for the target query AND refuses drafts targeting local/service queries. Same intent found → don’t publish, report instead. Ties → Erik decides. One Slack message beats months of split rankings. 6 Shared facts — NAP & claims (both sites, verbatim) Google reads both domains as one business, so these values must be byte-identical everywhere (schema, footers, city pages, GBP). Verified against Google Business Profile July 14, 2026: Address2025 Freeman Rd E, Milton, WA 98354 Phone(253) 922-5793 Google rating4.9★ · 187 reviews (as of Jul 14, 2026 — recheck when quoted; real review texts only) HoursMon–Fri 8:30am–5:00pm (GBP shows “Opens 9 AM” — Erik: confirm which is right, then align GBP + both sites) Founded1977 — “the Northwest’s original embroidery shop” Claims contract: turnaround times, minimums, and same-day options must read the same on .net city pages, .net FAQs, and teamnwca tools/pages. Before Mehar publishes his first city page, confirm the real numbers once and reuse verbatim. One business can’t tell Google two different stories. Anyone spotting a mismatch on either site flags it to Erik. 7 Scoreboard & checkpoints Review monthly (with Mehar’s report) Non-brand organic clicks, both properties (Search Console) — the real growth number; brand searches don’t count. Quote requests / form fills from organic, whichever site they land on — it’s one pipeline (watch Forms Inbox referrers). SEMrush keyword counts both domains — teamnwca baseline 42 (Jul 12, 2026); .net decline vs its −9%/mo baseline. Cross-domain click-through — .net → teamnwca catalog clicks and the reverse. Zero-cannibalization check — no query where both domains sit on pages 1–3 with the same intent; if found, pick one owner and de-optimize/301 the other. October 2026 checkpoint Three months of curves on both sites, reviewed together. Success looks like: teamnwca: 12+ posts live and indexed; style-number queries ranking (those move fastest); keyword count climbing steadily from 42. .net: money pages moving page 2 → page 1 on the target commercial terms; local pack visibility for “near me” searches; informational bleed slowed. Business: quote requests arriving with blog/product referrers. Then: revisit the long-term one-domain-vs-two question with data (deliberately deferred — no merge for now, Erik’s call July 12). 8 Reference shelf — the source documents Canonical copies live in the Pricing Index repo; the same four HTML docs were emailed to Mehar July 14, 2026. NWCA runs two websites, and Google knows they are the same business — both carry sameAs schema pointing at each other and share the same name, address, and phone (entity stitching, live on both sides since July 12, 2026). That is deliberate: it pools brand authority into one knowledge-graph entity.

The one consequence that shapes everything: if both sites publish pages chasing the same search query, Google splits ranking strength between them and often ranks neither on page 1. We watched this happen on .net itself — “custom embroidery near me” split across two of its own pages held both on page 2. Across two domains it is worse. So the rule is not “compete gently”; it is never compete at all: every query class has exactly one owner, and the other site links to it.

Division of labor: Mehar (umehar56@gmail.com) runs .net per the Recovery Roadmap. Claude runs teamnwca per this page (weekly blog autopilot + product/brand SEO). Erik owns gray-area calls and relays questions between the two. The full doctrine was decided July 13–14, 2026 (“Lane Split v2”) and sent to Mehar as a 4-document packet on July 14.

pages.title: ShopWorks Data Entry Guide | Northwest Custom Apparel
pages.mainText: Staff Dashboard / Data Entry Guide Service Prices Print ShopWorks Data Entry Guide Clean data entry = clean quotes = correct revenue tracking. For Nika Lao & Taneisha Clark. STOP — Bad Habits to Break 1 Stop using separator labels as line items What's wrong: Entering "Transfer", "EMB", "Embroidery", or "DTF" as line items with a blank part number. These aren't services — they're labels that confuse the system. Real examples: Order #136554 (Cardinal Baths): "Transfer" entered as a line item separator Order #136557 (Cosco Fire): "Embroidery" and "Transfer" labels mixed as items Order #136479: "EMB" as a standalone item Do this instead: Put placement/method notes in the ShopWorks Notes field at the bottom of the order. 2 Stop using person names as line item dividers What's wrong: Entering "Michael Bunce - Tonal Logo" or "Chad Matthew - Tonal Logo" as line items with blank part numbers to group products by person. Real example: Order #136556 (Cosco Fire #1): Multiple person-name dividers between product groups Do this instead: Use a single note in the Notes field: "Michael: items 1-3, Chad: items 4-6". 3 Stop leaving Part Number blank on priced items What's wrong: Entering a service description with a price but no part number. The system can't track revenue or classify the service correctly. Real examples: Order #136562 (Fire Buffs): "Sew-on" at $12.50 with empty PN — should be SEG Order #136271: "Laser - Customer's Supplies" at $12.50 with empty PN Do this instead: Every priced line item needs a part number. See the Service Code Reference below. 4 Stop using legacy/wrong service codes What's wrong: Typing old codes or typos that the system has to guess about. The parser fixes 13 known typos automatically, but don't rely on it. Real examples: "AONOGRAM" (typo), "EJB" (legacy), "SETUP FEE" (vague), "NAMES" (wrong) Do this instead: Use the exact codes from the Service Code Reference. See the Alias Reference at the bottom for what the system auto-corrects. 5 Stop mixing decoration types on one order What's wrong: Same ShopWorks order has both "Transfer" items and "Embroidery" items. The quote builder can only generate one type of quote per order. Do this instead: Create separate ShopWorks orders — one per decoration method. If a customer needs embroidery AND transfers, that's two orders. 6 Stop entering AL when you mean Full Back What's wrong: Using AL (Additional Logo) at $40-120/piece. AL is for small secondary logos ($7-10/pc). If the price is that high, it's a Full Back embroidery job. Real examples: Order #136257 (Little Wheels QMA): AL at $120/pc — this is not an Additional Logo Order #136429 (CCNW Commercial): AL at $12.50 — likely a Full Back job What It IsPart NumberPrice Range Small secondary logoAL$7-10/pc Full back embroideryDECG-FBStitch-count based 7 Stop entering addresses with lowercase states or typos What's wrong: "Wa" instead of "WA", "Antt:" instead of "Attn:". The tax lookup system needs a clean uppercase state code to determine the correct tax rate. Do this instead: Always use 2-letter uppercase state codes (WA, OR, CA, AK). Spell "Attn:" correctly. Include the full 5-digit ZIP code. START — Correct Practices 1 Always provide a Part Number for every priced line item No exceptions. If a line item has a dollar amount, it needs a part number. Refer to the Service Code Reference below. 2 Use the Notes field for non-product information The ShopWorks Notes field (bottom of the order) is for: Placement instructions ("Left Chest", "Back Logo") Person name groupings ("Michael: items 1-3") Method labels ("This section is Transfer") Special instructions ("Rush — need by Friday") None of these should be line items. 3 Follow the address format Company Name, Street Address, City, ST ZIP State: Always 2-letter uppercase (WA, OR, CA, AK — not "Wa") ZIP: Always 5-digit (or 5+4 with dash: 98402-1234) Attn: Spell it correctly if needed ("Attn: John Smith") 4 One decoration type per order Embroidery order → only embroidery items Transfer order → only transfer items DTG order → only DTG items If customer needs both → create two separate orders 5 Complete Design Numbers Design #:XXXXX - [full description] Include the design name so the quote builder can display it Don't leave trailing dashes with no description Example: Design #:39186 - Roadmen Car Club back logo 6 Correct size suffixes on part numbers SizeSuffixExample 2XL_2XPC54_2X 3XL_3XPC54_3X 4XL_4XPC54_4X 5XL_5X— 6XL_6X— One size_OSFACP90_OSFA Don't combine sizes: _4/5X should be separate items for 4XL and 5XL. Service Code Reference Fixed-Price Services Service Part Number 2026 Price Notes Loading prices... For tier-based pricing (DECG, AL, stitch surcharges), see the Service Price Cheat Sheet. Pre-Submit Checklist Check Before Saving Every Order Every line item has a Part Number (no blank PNs on priced items) No separator/label rows (Transfer, EMB, person names → moved to Notes) Correct service codes used (DD not "SETUP FEE", SEG not "Sew-on") Ship-to address: uppercase state + 5-digit ZIP One decoration type per order Design number has full description (no trailing dash) AL pricing is $7-10/pc range (if higher → probably Full Back, use DECG-FB) DECG pricing follows tier card (not flat $15-20) Digitizing is DD = $100 (not $50, not $150) Alias Reference Auto-Corrected Aliases The parser auto-corrects these, but entering the correct code saves time and avoids warnings: What Reps Type Parser Maps To What You Should Type AONOGRAMMONOGRAMMonogram NNAME / NNAMES / NAMEName/NumberName/Number NAMESMONOGRAMMonogram EJBFBDECG-FB FLAGALAL SETUPGRT-50GRT-50 SETUP FEEDDDD DESIGN PREPGRT-75GRT-75 EXCESS STITCHAS-GARMAS-Garm SEW / SEW-ONSEGSEG COLOR CHANGEColor ChgColor Chg — $15 screen-print fee Service prices loaded from API on page load.
